title: Imaging the Root Hair Morphology of Arabidopsis Seedlings in a Two-layer Microfluidic Platform
protocol: Spin coat epoxy-based negative photoresist onto a 4 inch diameter silicon wafer according to manufacturer's specifications to obtain a height of 20 µm.
Soft-bake the resist coated wafers for 4 min at 95 °C.
Allow wafer to cool for 5 min.
Expose the wafer to UV light for 15 s through a photomask in a UV contact aligner.
Post-exposure bake the wafer for 5 min at 95 °C.
Return the wafer to the spin coater and spin on a second layer of epoxy-based negative photoresist at 3,000 rpm to achieve a height of 150 - 200 µm.
Allow the wafer to rest for 5 min before transferring to a 95 °C hotplate for 45 min.
After baking on the hotplate, remove the wafer and allow the resist to cool and harden at room temperature for another 5 min on a flat level surface.
Align and expose the wafer to the second layer photomask for 30 s in a UV contact aligner.
Perform a post-exposure bake by placing the wafer on a hotplate for 15 min at 95 °C.
Allow the wafer to cool on a flat level surface for 5 min before developing.
Develop both resist layers simultaneously by placing the wafer into a plastic dish and submerging it in the appropriate developer.
Gently rock the dish occasionally for even washing of the wafer.
Rinse the wafer with isopropanol after 17 minutes.
Continue to rinse the wafer alternately with developer and IPA until any white film disappears.
Dry the patterned silicon wafer with nitrogen.
Expose the silicon wafer to an air plasma for 30 seconds in a plasma cleaner set on high.
Silanize the wafer with trichloro (1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluoro-n-octyl) silane at 85 °C for two hours in a chemical hood.
Pour a 10:1 ratio of polydimethylsiloxane to curing agent onto the silicon master wafer.
Degas the mixed PDMS in a vacuum chamber and then cure it in a 70 °C oven for one hour.
Cut the PDMS devices with a scalpel and peel them from the silicon master wafer.
Create seed and treatment inlets using a 1.5 mm biopsy punch, punching the seed inlet at a 45° angle to encourage root growth into the main channel.
Use clear adhesive tape to remove debris from the PDMS device.
Place the PDMS device design side down on a glass coverslip.
Autoclave the assembled devices.
Surface sterilize A. thaliana seeds with a solution of 30% commercially available bleach diluted in de-ionized water and 0.1% Triton X detergent for 7 min.
Wash seeds 4 times with sterile water.
Refrigerate microfuge tube overnight or up to a week at 4 °C.
Place sterilized devices in a vacuum degassing chamber.
Remove the devices from the vacuum chamber and immediately submerge them in a Petri dish filled with liquid ¼ strength plant-based media at pH 5.7.
Pull liquid through the inlets to fill the device using a pipette.
Ensure no air bubbles remain within channels by visual inspection.
Transfer individual devices to new dry Petri dishes.
Pour or pipette hot agar around the device until the agar level is almost flush with the top of the PDMS device.
Allow agar to solidify.
Transfer one sterilized seed to the inlet of each device using a small pipette in a sterile environment.
Cover the Petri dish with wax film.
Place the Petri dish in a light/dark cycling growth chamber or windowsill at room temperature.
Orient the Petri dish so that the devices are vertical.
Add the experimental treatment to each of the 8 side ports via pipette.
Reseal the Petri dish and return it to the growth chamber or windowsill.
Place the entire Petri dish containing the device and seedling under an inverted bright field microscope for lower resolution (4 - 20X) imaging.
Optimize lighting conditions by adjusting exposure times, lamp brightness, aperture, and light polarity.
Drive the stage to focus on the root or root hair(s) of interest.
Acquire a single time point or a time series of images.
To visualize growth of root hairs, image growing root hairs once per minute.
To visualize growth of the main root, acquire one image every 30 minutes.
Return the Petri dish and seedlings to the growth chamber or windowsill in a vertical position after imaging is complete.
Once the seedling has grown for a desired time, use forceps to remove coverslip and device from the agar.
Clean off the bottom of the coverslip using an ethanol-wetted laboratory tissue.
Apply immersion media recommended by the microscope lens manufacturer.
Place the coverslip on the microscope stage and raise the stage to contact the immersion media on the objective.
Optimize lighting conditions by adjusting exposure times, lamp brightness, aperture, and light polarity.
Drive the stage to the desired area and focus on root hair(s) of interest.
Use DIC for visualizing cytoplasmic streaming and fluorescence markers for organelle movement.
Acquire one image per minute to quantify root hair growth over time.
Minimize fluorescence exposure time while retaining an identifiable signal from organelles.
Acquire images of the organelles as quickly as possible based on the exposure time.
Use a live-cell imaging stage incubator to maintain ambient temperature and moisture for longer time-lapse imaging.
Once seedling has grown for desired time, remove the device and coverslip from the Petri dish.
Turn the device upside down and gently peel away the coverslip so that the root stays within the PDMS channel.
Proceed to use the PDMS device as a substrate for the root in higher resolution atomic force or scanning electron microscopy.
Deposit a thin (~20 nm) layer of chromium onto the root and surrounding PDMS using a Dual Gun Electron Beam Evaporation Chamber.
Transfer the root and PDMS device to a scanning electron microscope chamber.
Mount the PDMS device root side up on an AFM specimen holder.
Place the PDMS device on a flat reflective substrate before mounting it on the AFM specimen holder.
Secure a liquid well attachment on top of the PDMS device and fill it with water to keep the roots hydrated during imaging.
Load the specimen holder into the AFM.
Adjust the z-control for the thickness of the PDMS device.
Drive the cantilever to the region of interest on the root using a camera for guidance.
Align the laser with the tip of the cantilever.
Use cantilevers with spring constants of 0.01 or 0.03 N/m.
Slowly lower the scanning mechanism until the cantilever just makes contact with the sample.
Adjust the scan size for the desired region.
Choose a scan speed of 1 line/s with 256 voltage points per line.
Acquire the scan.
